Subject (in full) The Gold Bar Exchange.
Made by D. I. Ross Forwarded by Henry Robertson C.D.I.

The buying and selling of gold bars is
controlled by a very select ring, and as long as silver
remains the currency of China speculation on the gold
bar exchange will continue to exist. This is
the main reason for any business being possible.
Some gold is imported and some is mined in
China. A bar weighs ten ounces and is never sold
singly but in multiples of seven.
Business may be transacted by members of the
gold exchange either on their own behalf or acting
for clients. In deals regarding the latter both
the buyer and the seller pay the sum of taels 5 cents
commission per bar brokerage to the broker. This
is the authorized amount laid down but it is a
recognized fact that brokers demand considerably more
than this meagre figure.
The causes of fluctuation are numerous, chief
among them being, the value of the pound sterling,
U.S. dollars, yen, the current price of silver, ship-
ments of gold, the supply of gold on the market and the
demand for same. The price of gold bars is controlled
by the members of the gold bar exchange. Transactions
therefore depend entirely upon what figure the seller is
willing to accept and what the purchaser is prepared
to give. All matters relevant to the deal are taken
into consideration before the business is completed,
but in spite of these precautions errors in judgment
often occur.

金条的买卖受一个非常封闭的小圈子控制，只要白银仍是中国的货币，金条交易所的投机活动就会继续存在。这是任何业务得以进行的根本原因。部分黄金为进口，部分为中国本土开采。一根金条重十盎司，从不单根出售，而是以七的倍数出售。
交易所成员可以代表自己或代表客户进行交易。在代表客户的交易中，买卖双方需向经纪人支付每根金条5分银两的佣金。这是规定的标准金额，但众所周知，经纪人要求的费用远高于这一微薄的数字。
造成价格波动的原因众多，其中主要包括：英镑、美元、日元的价值，白银的现行价格，黄金运输量，市场黄金供应量以及需求量。金条价格由金条交易所成员控制。因此，交易完全取决于卖方愿意接受的价格和买方准备支付的价格。在完成交易前，所有与交易相关的事项均会被纳入考量，但尽管有这些预防措施，判断失误仍经常发生。

Translation of the Revised Regulations of the Shanghai Gold Stock
Exchange Co., Ltd.

Chapter I: General Rules

Art. 1 This Exchange is organized in accordance with the regulations
of the Products Exchange and is named "The Shanghai Gold
Stock Exchange Ltd."

Art. 2 This Exchange was promoted by managers of various firms
registered with the Gold Dealers' Association and established
with the sanction of the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce.

Art. 3 This Exchange is situated in the International Settlement.

Art. 4 This Exchange will function for ten years from the date of
registration with the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce,
on the expiration of which period it may petition the Ministry
for prolongation of the period.

Chapter II Dealings

Art. 5 This Exchange deals solely in gold transactions , either
"spot" or "forward", with the object of assuring safety in
dealings and the development of commerce.

Art. 6 The notifications of the Exchange will be published in the
Chinese vernacular papers fixed by the Exchange. However,
matters concerning transactions will only be displayed in
the Exchange.

Chapter III Capital & Shares

Art. 7 The total amount of Capital of the Exchange is fixed at
$1,500,000 Shanghai currency, which is divided into
100,000 shares, that is to say, one share is worth $15.00.

Art. 8 The money for the shares is paid to the Exchange at one
payment.

Art. 9 The share coupons of the Exchange are of five kinds, namely
"1 share", "5 shares", "10 shares", "50 shares" and "100 shares"
coupons. On issuance, each coupon should bear the chop of
the Exchange, and signed and chopped by the chairman and
two members of the Standing Committee of the Exchange.

《上海金业交易所有限公司修订章程》译文

第一章：总则

第一条 本交易所依据物品交易所条例组织成立，命名为“上海金业交易所有限公司”。

第二条 本交易所由在金业同业公会注册的各商号经理人发起，并经农商部批准设立。

第三条 本交易所位于公共租界。

第四条 本交易所自向农商部注册之日起运营十年，期满后可向农商部申请延期。

第二章 交易

第五条 本交易所专事黄金交易，包括“现货”或“远期”，旨在确保交易安全及促进商业发展。

第六条 交易所通告将刊登于交易所指定的中文白话报纸上。然而，有关交易的事项仅在交易所内公示。

第三章 资本与股份

第七条 本交易所资本总额定为上海规元1,500,000元，分为100,000股，即每股价值15.00元。

第八条 股款须一次性缴付给交易所。

第九条 本交易所股票分为五种，即“1股”、“5股”、“10股”、“50股”和“100股”票面。发行时，每张股票应加盖交易所印章，并由交易所主席及常务委员会两名委员签名并盖章。

价值关平银2.16亿两的金条
由“美元轮船公司”轮船装运
官方举措
政府尚未显示将解除
对黄金属的出口禁令

在南京国民政府财政部长宋子文先生的授权下，价值关平银2.16亿两的金条昨日由中国中央银行通过“美元轮船公司”（Dollar Line）的“克利夫兰总统号”（S.S. President Cleveland）轮船运往美国政府位于旧金山的铸币局。据悉，后续还将有其他批次装运。

这是南京当局实施出口禁令以来，黄金首次被运送出境。此前，当地个人和团体不时进行不规则且非法的装运，大多运往日本，但昨日的金条运输获得了国民政府的批准，实际上代表的是官方资金。

谣言丛生

中国中央银行在当地金库中拥有异常大量的金条，这一事实在过去两周引发了持续的谣言，称正考虑向美国装运黄金。然而，《字林西报》在金融和保险界的查询未能获得任何关于此类转移的证实，昨日有明确说法称，直到“克利夫兰总统号”启程前往旧金山前，并未进行此类装运。

根据来自南京的消息，这批金银可能被兑换成金元，从而赚取利息，否则若金条仍由银行持有，这部分利息将会损失。就本地金条交易而言，预计不会产生任何反响，因为据称此次装运纯属政府行为，丝毫未表明有意解除对黄金属的禁令。

官方机构

宋子文先生除了担任国民政府财政部长外，还是中国中央银行董事会主席。该银行是一家直接受南京控制的政府机构，其董事局和监察委员会均由中国官员组成。这是全国唯一获准处理金条并可在特别许可下出售金条的金融机构。

Gambling in Gold Bars

Judging by the number of regulations and sheer gambling one is tempted to think that the most difficult of economic problems is to stop speculation.

Probably the only really effective test is to see whether the “seller” can actually deliver the goods. But as it often happens that the last thing in the world which the “buyer” wishes is to take actual delivery of that which he has “bought,” the simplest test is not very often applied.

Recent rumors that the Chinese Government intended to take drastic action in regard to exercising control over gold bar transactions have been now confirmed.

The Central Political Council has drawn up a series of regulations to this end which the Ministry of Industry has been instructed strictly to enforce immediately.

The object of these restrictions is to make it impossible for any but genuine buyers and sellers to dabble in gold bar transactions. Whether this can be done effectively in the manner proposed remains to be seen.

If it can, Shanghai will be freed from one of the far too many speculative activities which make legitimate business difficult, especially at times like the present, when economic conditions generally are so unsettled as to encourage gambling.

Under the regulations just issued from Nanking, brokers on the Shanghai Gold Bar Exchange and the Shanghai Stock and Produce Exchange (which also handles gold bar transactions) are forbidden to do business with any but bonafide exporters of silk or dealers in foreign exchange. The penalty for infringement of this order is withdrawal of the broker’s license, and he also will be severely punished by the Ministry of Industry.

In addition, brokers in future must receive 50 per cent of the price of the gold bars in cash down, and if they accept less than 50 per cent of the amount agreed, 50 per cent of the difference...

...additional security must be given. This is intended to put a stop to the practice of buying with selling which consists mainly of betting on a rise or fall in the market without any intention of actual delivery.

There are many other new rules and restrictions, the most important being that providing for government action—either on its own initiative or at the request of the Exchange—which gives it power to remove any broker who are “dealing purely to manipulate” or corner the market.

Interpretation by the government may take the shape of ordering the suspension of business entirely, or imposing additional restrictions.

It is to be hoped that the enforcement of these regulations by the Ministry of Industry will have an immediate effect in checking the wild method of gambling which has become so common in recent months, and that the authorities will exercise the necessary vigilance in seeing that the authorities do their duty.

Everybody knows that the gold bar market is largely speculative; the same applies to the do not understand many of the intricacies of the bullion ring pretend to know all about it. It is, of course, a perfectly legitimate form of business when engaged in honestly, but the system of fundamental speculative folly on the exchange is purely speculative.

If the matter stopped there, the position might be met by imposing a heavy tax on these transactions, but the problem is far, far beyond the walls of the Exchange, extending to all business what.

Gambling in gold bars has a very bad effect upon local trade relations, and therefore indirectly affects exchange operations and foreign commerce.

With reference to the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce’s recently published list of complaints in regard to various business grievances, it is probable that some of them would disappear if the gold bar gambling were stopped, and perhaps some of the other complaints would also be remedied if the general tone of business were improved.

金条投机

鉴于规章的数量之多以及纯粹的赌博性质，人们不禁认为，最棘手的经济问题莫过于遏制投机。

或许唯一真正有效的检验标准，是看“卖方”是否实际交付货物。但由于“买方”往往最不愿意实际提取其所“购买”之物，这种最简单的检验方法并不常被采用。

此前有关中国政府打算对金条交易实施严格控制的传闻，现已得到证实。

中央政治会议已为此制定了一系列规章，并指示实业部立即严格执行。

这些限制措施的目的是使除真实买卖双方之外的任何人无法涉足金条交易。拟议的方式能否有效做到这一点，尚待观察。

如果能够做到，上海将摆脱过多投机活动中的其中一项，这些活动使得正当商业经营变得困难，尤其是在当前经济状况普遍动荡、助长赌博风气的时刻。

根据南京刚刚颁布的规章，上海金业交易所和上海证券物品交易所（也处理金条交易）的经纪人被禁止与除生丝真实出口商或外汇交易商以外的任何人进行交易。违反此令的惩罚是吊销经纪人执照，并将受到实业部的严厉惩处。

此外，经纪人今后必须收取金条价格的50%作为现金首付，如果他们接受的金额低于约定金额的50%，则需就差额部分的50%……

……提供额外担保。此举旨在制止以卖空买空为主的、无意实际交割而仅赌市场涨跌的做法。

还有许多其他新规和限制，其中最重要的是规定政府采取行动——无论是主动还是应交易所请求——赋予其权力以移除任何“纯粹为了操纵”或垄断市场的经纪人。

政府的解释可能采取命令完全停业或施加额外限制的形式。

希望实业部执行这些规章能立即产生效果，遏制近几个月来如此猖獗的疯狂赌博方式，并希望当局保持必要的警惕，确保相关部门履行职责。

众所周知，金条市场很大程度上是投机性的；同样适用于那些不懂金银交易圈许多复杂内情却假装无所不知的人。当然，如果诚实经营，这是一种完全合法的商业形式，但交易所基于根本性投机愚行的体系则是纯粹的投机。

如果事情仅止于此，或许可以通过对这些交易征收重税来解决，但问题远远超出了交易所的范围，波及所有商业领域。

金条投机对本地贸易关系有非常恶劣的影响，因此间接影响汇兑操作和对外贸易。

参照上海总商会最近发布的关于各种商业不满的投诉清单，如果停止金条赌博，其中一些投诉可能会消失；如果整体商业风气得到改善，或许其他一些投诉也会得到补救。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 5, 1931

Government and
Nanking Road
Prince of Wales' Tour
Gold Bar Exchange
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."
SIR,—The communication in your paper about the measures devised by the government for the control of the Gold Bar Exchange, I am sure, must have been read by all business men and industrialists with a sigh of relief. I have however my doubts about the ability of the authorities, as, only last week the measure for the closing of the Exchange was contemplated but nothing further was heard about the matter.
Whatever be the intention of the government to control gold bar exchange will not serve any purpose if speculation does not cease. The authorities have to respond to the call of the hour.
Exchanges for commodities, are vital to trade and industry, enabling operators to hedge against possible rise or fall of the commodity prices.
Why cannot the Chinese government take courage and devise stringent measures to eradicate once for all the malignant canker of speculation that is fast corroding the body of China?
The very first step the authorities should take is to penalise very heavily these few arch-speculators. Last week we read that Italy deported from the country, a very influential and wealthy industrialist and financier, for his speculative operations detrimental to the country. France did the same last month.
China for the moment practically rules the silver market of the world
and if the sales and purchases of this metal were made and regulated according to the requirements of the trade and currency, the oscillation of the value of the Tael would form a correct barometer of the country's commerce with the outside world. But the barometer is disturbed and influenced by the sullied atmosphere of speculation emanating from the Gold Bar Exchange.
If the authorities would not or could not close this Exchange altogether, why should they not take up the question of foreign exchanges in their hands, by establishing a "Valuta" bureau, through which within all exchange banks should be made to get valutas on behalf of their clients, who in their turn should prove to the banks the bona fides of their exchange operations through documentary evidence proving genuine business transactions? This step will automatically clear cut speculation and create the stability of the value of the Tael.
In similar cases, immediately after the war, both France and Italy adopted this measure and at a later stage fixed their currency—Franc and Lira—at a certain value, basing such fixation on their gold holdings.
China is already burdened with the bad effects of her civil wars, but the effects of the war against Tael, will soon throw the country down into the abyss of ruin and chaos.
Stabilization of the currency means flourishing trade and good trade means prosperity to the country. Banditry and Communism will disappear at the sight of prosperity, as there would be ample occupation for the masses in the fields and in factories.
China has enough resources of silver and other metals and needs only a stable currency which will bring about prosperity.

(Signed) Chas. and M. B.'s)

《字林西报》，1931年2月5日，星期四

政府与
南京路
威尔士亲王巡访
金业交易所

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——贵报上关于政府 devised 控制金业交易所措施的通讯，我相信所有商人和工业家读后都如释重负。然而，我对当局的能力存有疑虑，因为就在上周，人们还在酝酿关闭交易所的措施，但此后便再无下文。

无论政府控制金条交易的意图如何，如果投机不停止，都将无济于事。当局必须回应时代的呼唤。

商品交易所对贸易和工业至关重要，使经营者能够对冲商品价格可能上涨或下跌的风险。

中国政府为何不能鼓起勇气，制定严厉措施，彻底根除正在迅速腐蚀中国肌体的投机这一恶性毒瘤？

当局应采取的第一步是对少数头号投机者处以重罚。上周我们读到，意大利因一位极具影响力和财富的工业家及金融家的投机操作损害国家利益，将其驱逐出境。法国上月也采取了同样行动。

中国目前实际上主宰着世界白银市场，如果这种金属的买卖能按照贸易和货币的需求进行和规范，银两价值的波动将成为衡量中国与外部世界贸易状况的正确晴雨表。但是，这个晴雨表受到了源自金业交易所的污浊投机气氛的干扰和影响。

如果当局不愿或不能完全关闭该交易所，为何不通过建立“外汇局”（Valuta bureau）将外汇问题掌握在自己手中，要求所有外汇银行通过该局代表客户获取外汇，而客户则需通过证明真实商业交易的单据证据，向银行证明其外汇操作的真实性？这一步骤将自动清除投机，并创造银两价值的稳定性。

在类似情况下，战后法国和意大利立即采取了这一措施，并在后期根据其黄金储备将货币——法郎和里拉——固定在一定价值上。

中国已经背负着内战带来的不良后果，但针对银两的战争所带来的后果，很快就会将这个国家推入毁灭和混乱的深渊。

货币稳定意味着贸易繁荣，良好的贸易意味着国家繁荣。匪患和共产主义将在繁荣景象面前消失，因为大众在田野和工厂中将会有充足的就业机会。

中国拥有足够的白银和其他金属资源，只需要一种能带来繁荣的稳定货币。

（签名）Chas. and M. B.'s)

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 5, 1931

LOCAL EXCHANGES
The letter appearing in the correspondence columns to-day regarding the Gold Bar Exchange can only be accepted as a personal expression of opinion. To say that "the Exchange has no legitimate object and is nothing more than a gambling house" is unfair, and if the writer of the letter had taken the trouble to ascertain the opinions of exchange brokers actively engaged in fixing rates of exchange for importing and exporting firms, he would have found that at times the speculation proceeding there has been the medium of securing certain more favourable rates for remittances than in these difficult times of trade would otherwise have been available. That gambling in addition to what may be described as legitimate speculation occurs is undeniable, and the regulations recently issued by the Nanking Government have been devised with a view to suppressing it. To blame the Gold Bar Exchange, however, for all the evils in local business is hardly correct. The crimes of Kiukiang Road are not as all-embracing as the correspondent appears to believe.
It will be noted that the writer of the letter mentions the case of a cotton mill having closed its doors "owing to the evils of the speculative mania of the owners." One of the best informed firms on the local cotton and yarn situation, Messrs. J. Spurrier & Co., dealt with this matter in their report published in the "North-China Daily News" last Saturday, when they said:—
The yarn market has been quite steady during the early part of the week, as one of the Chinese mills, due to financial difficulties, went into voluntary liquidation, the proprietor of which mill was one of the largest operators in yarn and cotton (bear side) on the Cotton Goods Exchange. In order to settle bears and particularly the mill in question to cover its shorts by net sales in

the market, the Exchange put into effect an order to demand a special margin of Tls. 10 cash per bale on any new purchases, and hence the buying forces were restricted.
It has to be emphasized that the Cotton Goods Exchange is entirely separate from the Gold Exchange, and it is certainly of interest to note that the authorities there at once took action on their own initiative to prevent a further dislocation of normal business conditions.
Where the writer of the letter is in a sense correct is that operations on the Cotton Goods Exchange are influenced by those on the Gold Bar Exchange. For instance yesterday when observers of the market expected to see the price of cotton yarn lower, they found it higher because there is a belief in Kiukiang Road that the price of gold bars is going to advance to still further heights. In other economic systems, however, one finds practically a similar condition of affairs existing, commodities being under the influence of money rates and the prices of other commodities. Of course there is no doubt that at times Shanghai—as was probably only natural when growing up to its still aspiréd condition of maturity—went mad over the prospect of making untold wealth by the establishment of exchanges for every purpose in the world, no commodity being so insignificant that people could not be found to establish an exchange for it, but that fever quickly and radically cured itself. What must now be strived at is to bring the present exchanges into line with the soundest foreign practice, making them an aid to commerce as they should be, with regulations which sane Chinese business men know perfectly well how to devise to meet their own special conditions, to eliminate as far as humanly possible violent disruptions of the normal channels of trade.

P.S. (b. and Sp. bris)

form of return. J.H.

本地汇兑

今日刊登在通信栏中关于金条交易所的信件，只能被视为一种个人观点的表达。称“该交易所没有合法目标，不过是一个赌场”是不公平的；如果写信人肯费心去了解一下那些积极为进出口商行确定汇率的汇兑经纪人的意见，他就会发现，在贸易困难的时期，那里进行的投机活动有时反而成为获得比通常更有利的汇款汇率的途径。不可否认，除了可称为合法投机之外的赌博行为确实存在，而南京政府最近颁布的规章正是为了抑制这种现象。然而，将本地商业中的所有弊病都归咎于金条交易所，则并不正确。九江路的罪孽并不像这位通讯员所认为的那样包罗万象。

值得注意的是，信中提到一家棉纺厂因“业主受投机狂热之害”而关门停业。本地对棉纱行情最为了解的公司之一，J. Spurrier & Co.（音译），在其上周六发表于《字林西报》的报告中处理了这一问题，他们说道：——

本周初纱市相当平稳，因为一家华资纱厂因财务困难进入自愿清算程序，该厂业主是纱布交易所上最大的纱花空头操作者之一。为了结清空头头寸，特别是为了让该厂通过市场净卖出平仓其空头，交易所实施了一项命令，要求任何新买入每包需缴纳现银10两的特别保证金，因此买盘力量受到限制。

必须强调，纱布交易所与金业交易所是完全分开的，当然有趣的是，注意到那里的当局立即主动采取行动，以防止正常商业秩序进一步混乱。

从某种意义上说，写信人正确之处在于，纱布交易所的操作受到金条交易所操作的影响。例如昨天，当市场观察员预期棉纱价格会下跌时，却发现价格上涨，因为九江路方面相信金条价格将进一步攀升至更高水平。然而，在其他经济体系中，人们也发现实际上存在类似的情况，即商品受到货币利率和其他商品价格的影响。当然，毫无疑问，上海有时——这在它成长为其所向往的成熟状态的过程中可能是自然的——曾疯狂地希望通过建立各种目的的交易所来获取无数财富，没有任何商品微不足道到找不到人为其建立交易所的地步，但这种狂热很快且彻底地自行消退了。现在必须努力的是使目前的交易所符合最健全的外国惯例，使其成为应有的商业辅助工具，并制定理性的中国商人完全知道如何设计以适应其自身特殊情况的规章，以尽可能消除对正常贸易渠道的剧烈干扰。

附言。（b. and Sp. bris）
信息及
报表格式。J.H.
31年1月5日。

THE MINISTRY OF INDUSTRY & THE GOLD BAR EXCHANGE

The China Times and other local newspapers
publish the following report :-

The Ministry of Industry has sent to the
Municipality of Greater Shanghai the following ten
measures passed by the Central Political Meeting and
directs that they be transmitted to the Shanghai Gold
Bar Exchange and the Shanghai Bond and Exchange
to be observed by them:-
(1) By order of the Ministry, brokers must not
buy or sell on behalf of persons who are not in the
international money exchange business or export
business.
(2) Any broker who violates the order will
have his licence withdrawn by the Ministry and a fine
will be imposed. The Gold Exchange will also be
fined if it be discovered to have concealed the
offence.
(3) The amount to be deposited by both the
buyer and the seller must exceed one-tenth of the
value of the purchase or sale and a further deposit
will be required if the difference in price reaches
50% of the amount of the original deposit. Offenders
will be severely dealt with.
(4) The Ministry will ask for documents of
purchase or sale and for a further deposit in case
there is a large increase or decrease in the value
of gold or silver.
(5) The committeemen and staff of the Gold
Exchange are strictly prohibited to conspire with
brokers in business transactions. Offenders will
be dismissed and severely punished in other ways.
(6) Brokers are not allowed to undertake
speculation business personally.
(7) In case the abnormal increase or decrease
in the value of gold had been exclusively managed by
brokers, the Ministry will close down the Exchange
when it is deemed fit.
(8) The Exchange must publish every day the
market rates and average rates and the amount of
business done by brokers. This is to be checked
by supervising officers.
(9) Brokers should every day make reports
of the amounts and the kinds of business transacted
on behalf of others.
(10) The supervising officers have the right
at any time to investigate the books of Exchanges
and the contracts entered into by brokers on behalf
of clients.

实业部与金条交易所

《时事新报》及其他本地报纸
刊登如下报道：-

实业部已向大上海市政府发送由中央政治会议通过的以下十项措施，并指示将其转达给上海金业交易所和上海证券物品交易所，令其遵守：-
(1) 奉部令，经纪人不得为非从事国际汇兑业务或出口业务的人士买卖。
(2) 任何违反此令的经纪人将被实业部吊销执照并处以罚款。如果发现金业交易所隐瞒违规行为，也将对其处以罚款。
(3) 买卖双方存入的保证金金额必须超过买卖价值的十分之一，如果价差达到原保证金金额的50%，则需追加保证金。违规者将受到严厉惩处。
(4) 如果金银价值出现大幅涨跌，实业部将要求提供买卖凭证并追加保证金。
(5) 严禁金业交易所的委员及职员在交易中与经纪人串通。违规者将被撤职并受到其他严厉惩罚。
(6) 经纪人不得亲自从事投机业务。
(7) 如果金银价值的异常涨跌完全由经纪人操纵，实业部将在认为适当时关闭交易所。
(8) 交易所必须每日公布市场行情、平均行情以及经纪人的成交量。这将由监理员进行核查。
(9) 经纪人应每日报告代他人交易的金额和业务种类。
(10) 监理员有权随时调查交易所的账簿以及经纪人代表客户签订的合同。

Shanghai Times - February 1, 1931.

Gold Bar Speculation To
Be Restricted Under New
Regulations By Nanking

BROKERS PROHIBITED BUYING OR SELLING
OTHER THAN FOR BONA FIDE EXPORTERS
OR DEALERS IN FOREIGN EXCHANGE

10 PER CENT. OBLIGATORY MARGIN MUST BE
INCREASED WITH BIG FLUCTUATIONS

Shanghai Gold Bar Exchange And Shanghai Stock
And Produce Exchange Ordered Imme-
diately To Enforce Regulations

The National Government of China has decided to regulate speculation in gold bars, and ten articles have been drawn up for transmission to the Shanghai Gold Bar Exchange and the Shanghai Stock and Produce Exchange for immediate observance. The measures approved by the Central Political Council strictly prohibit brokers buying or selling on behalf of parties not bona fide exporters or dealers in foreign exchange, and the names of people engaging in transactions are to be submitted daily for examination. Violation of this order will mean that brokers will lose their licences and be severely punished, and exchanges who do not report transactions fully or otherwise connive with breaches of the new laws will be dealt with.

Article three stipulates that not less than ten per cent. shall be deposited by the buyer and seller as margin money, and in the event of fluctuations in the market quotation exceeding 50 per cent. of the margin money an additional deposit shall be paid. Brokers may not undertake transactions outside the exchange, while exchange business, or only forward transactions, may be ordered to be temporarily suspended when there is wild boosting or depression of quotations.

NANKING, Jan. 31.—A set of regulations governing the regulation of gold bar speculation, consisting of 10 articles, has been formally approved by the Central Political Council and handed down to the Ministry of Industry for strict enforcement.

It is understood that the regulations will be transmitted to the exchanges concerned (the Shanghai Gold Bar Exchange and the Shanghai Stock and Produce Exchange, in which gold bar transactions are also conducted) for immediate observance.

Curb Reckless Speculation

It is believed that with the enforcement of the new regulations, reckless speculation in gold bars on the part of the unscrupulous may be curbed.

The ten measures are as follows:—

1.—Brokers shall henceforth be prohibited from undertaking any transactions outside of the exchange concerned. Strict vigilance shall also be maintained over the enforcement of this provision by the Ministry's supervisor.

2.—Brokers found guilty of violating the preceding stipulation shall be deprived of their business licence and severely punished by the Ministry. Exchanges engaged in gold bar transactions which wilfully abstain from reporting, or otherwise connive with, such breach of the law, upon detection, shall likewise be dealt with.

Margin Money

3.—The "margin" money to be deposited by the buyer and seller shall not be less than 10 per cent. of the amount mutually agreed upon. In the event, however, of the fluctuations in the market quotation having exceeded 50 per cent. of the "margin" money, an additional deposit should immediately be paid. Violation of this rule shall be dealt with severely.

4.—During times of violent market fluctuations, the Ministry may issue special orders requiring an increase in the legal percentage of "margin" money and the payment of additional deposit by the parties concerned.

5.—Directors as well as officials and employees of the exchanges shall be strictly prohibited from engaging in gold bar transactions in collusion with the brokers, nor shall they violate this stipulation under any circumstances. Any breach thereof shall be dealt with severely.

6.—Brokers shall not be permitted to undertake any transactions outside of the exchange concerned.

7.—At times of wild fluctuations in the value of gold and silver, or when it is discovered that certain unscrupulous brokers are wilfully boosting or depressing quotations to manipulate or corner the market, or when it is believed that a crisis is likely to be caused without any satisfactory way of saving the situation, then the Ministry may, either on its own accord or upon the petition of the exchanges, order the temporary suspension of business of the exchanges or the suspension of forward transactions.

8.—Exchanges engaged in gold bar dealings shall be required to submit to the Supervisor for examination daily returns of the quotations and average quotation for the day as well as the amount and period of the transactions booked by their brokers for examination.

9.—All brokers shall likewise be required to submit for examination daily returns of the names of their clients, amount and period of transactions booked on their behalf, as well as the trades in which their clients are engaged.

《上海泰晤士报》 - 1931年2月1日。

南京新规将限制
金条投机

禁止经纪人为非真实出口商
或外汇交易商买卖

波动剧烈时必须增加
10%的强制保证金

命令上海金业交易所和上海证券物品交易所
立即执行规定

中国政府已决定规范金条投机行为，并制定了十条规定，发送给上海金业交易所和上海证券物品交易所，要求立即遵守。经中央政治委员会批准的措施严格禁止经纪人为非真实出口商或外汇交易商的一方进行买卖，参与交易的人员名单须每日提交审查。违反此令意味着经纪人将失去执照并受到严厉惩罚，未充分报告交易或以其他方式纵容违反新法律的交易所将受到处理。

第三条规定，买方和卖方必须存入不少于百分之十的款项作为保证金，如果市场报价波动超过保证金的百分之五十，则应支付额外保证金。经纪人不得在场外进行交易，而当出现疯狂哄抬或压低报价时，可命令暂停交易所业务或仅暂停远期交易。

南京，1月31日。—一套由10条组成的管理金条投机的规定已正式获得中央政治委员会批准，并下达给实业部严格执行。

据悉，这些规定将转交给有关交易所（上海金业交易所和上海证券物品交易所，后者也进行金条交易）立即遵守。

遏制盲目投机

人们相信，随着新规定的执行，无良之徒对金条的盲目投机可能会得到遏制。

这十项措施如下：—

1.—从此禁止经纪人在有关交易所之外进行任何交易。实业部监理员也将对此规定的执行保持严格警惕。

2.—被发现违反前述规定的经纪人将被剥夺营业执照并受到实业部的严厉惩罚。从事金条交易的交易所若故意不报告或以其他方式纵容此类违法行为，一经查实，也将同样受到处理。

保证金

3.—买方和卖方存入的“保证金”不得少于双方约定金额的10%。但是，如果市场报价波动超过“保证金”的50%，应立即支付额外保证金。违反此规则将受到严厉惩处。

4.—在市场剧烈波动期间，实业部可发布特别命令，要求提高法定“保证金”比例，并要求相关方支付额外保证金。

5.—严禁交易所董事以及官员和雇员与经纪人勾结从事金条交易，在任何情况下均不得违反此规定。任何违反行为将受到严厉惩处。

6.—不允许经纪人在有关交易所之外进行任何交易。

7.—在金银价值剧烈波动时，或者发现某些无良经纪人故意哄抬或压低报价以操纵或垄断市场时，或者认为可能引发危机且无任何令人满意的挽救办法时，实业部可自行或应交易所请求，命令暂时停止交易所业务或暂停远期交易。

8.—从事金条交易的交易所须每日向监理员提交当日行情和平均行情以及其经纪人记录的交易量和期限的日报表，以供审查。

9.—所有经纪人也须每日提交其客户姓名、代其记录的交易量和期限以及客户所从事行业的日报表，以供审查。

10.—[原文不清]

N.C.D.News - January 28,1931.

THE GOLD EXCHANGE
During the past few days
rumours have been current—not
by any means for the first time—
that the Chinese Government
intends to close the Shanghai
Gold Bar Exchange. It is
worthy of note that in the
Exchange little agitation has
been caused through this report,
and it is considered much more
likely that what Nanking has in
anticipation is a measure of
restriction on the transactions
undertaken. Kiukiang Road's
influence on the exchange posi-
tion is undoubtedly very great,
and it has been noted that opera-
tors there have been able to
force exchange up when the
price of silver has gone down
and vice versa, but this has
rather demonstrated the weak-
ness of silver as a metal than
anything else. There are many
different opinions regarding the
position of Kiukiang Road as a
factor in the economic life of
China: at times it has been
described as controlling the
silver markets of the world,
which is true up to a point, and
the amount of speculation pro-
ceeding there has also been
described as colossal. If, how-
ever, the opinion of one of the
best known brokers in Shanghai
is correct the amount of specula-
tion is nothing in comparison
with what goes on in the money
markets of London and New
York.
When it comes to dealing with
speculation it is essential that
it should not be mixed up with
gambling. The courts both in
England and America have
differentiated between the two,
and on the question of specula-
tion Mr. Hartley Withers, the
well-known writer on economic
subjects has some very interest-
ing sentences in his book entitled
"War and Lombard Street." He
says:—
Now speculation is not a vice
in itself. It is a stupid way of
losing one's money, but the
speculator is quite a useful per-
son so long as he is not given
rope enough to allow him to
become a danger to other people.
He helps to make a free market,
and he provides lodgings for new
issues until such time as the real
investor comes and buys them
and puts them away with the
money he has saved.
Obviously in any legislation it
may have in contemplation re-
garding Kiukiang Road the
Government ought to be guided
by a statement of the functions
of speculation such as this.
At present all that is known is
that there is talk in Nanking of
restricting the activities of the
exchange dealers, but if so it
will have to be done in a way
which will not inflict harm on
the community. By making a
free market, as Mr. Hartley
Withers says, merchants in the
past and to-day have been able
to secure rates for their bills
which in other circumstances
would not have been possible,
and that brings into prominence
the case where speculation
proves of benefit to the com-
mercial community. When, how-
ever, to refer again to the above
passage, speculation becomes a
danger, it is obviously time for
action. Probably the sanest
view to be obtained on the
matter is that of the exchange
brokers handling the bills of
importing and exporting firms,
and in the present state of
affairs it is interesting to note
that so far as can be learned the
freer market which the Ex-
change affords offsets the
greater evils. There is, how-
ever, an irresponsible element
with funds and knowledge of
small dimensions operating in
Kiukiang Road, and if it is the
elimination of this section that
the Government has in mind it
will not be acting without
justification.

file.

金条交易所
在过去几天里，有谣言流传——这绝非首次——称中国政府打算关闭上海金条交易所。值得注意的是，该交易所在此报告下并未引起多大骚动，人们认为南京方面更可能 anticipated（预期）采取的是对所做交易进行限制的措施。九江路对汇市行情的影响无疑非常大，且有人注意到，那里的操盘手能够在银价下跌时迫使汇率上涨，反之亦然，但这更多地证明了白银作为一种金属的弱势，而非其他。关于九江路作为中国经济生活因素的地位，众说纷纭：有时它被描述为控制着世界白银市场，这在一定程度上是属实的，而且那里的投机规模也被形容为巨大。然而，如果上海最知名的经纪人之一的观点是正确的，那么与伦敦和纽约货币市场上发生的情况相比，这里的投机量简直微不足道。

在处理投机问题时，必须将其与赌博区分开来。英国和美国的法院都对二者进行了区分，而在投机问题上，著名经济题材作家哈特利·威瑟斯（Hartley Withers）先生在其题为《战争与伦巴第街》（"War and Lombard Street"）的书中有一些非常有趣的论述。他说：—
现在，投机本身并不是一种恶习。这是一种愚蠢的赔钱方式，但只要不给投机者足够的余地使其成为对他人的危险，他们就完全是有益的人。他们有助于形成自由市场，并为新发行的证券提供栖身之所，直到真正的投资者前来购买并用其储蓄的资金将其持有。

显然，在政府可能考虑制定的任何关于九江路的立法中，都应以此类关于投机功能的陈述为指导。
目前所知的只是，南京方面有传言要限制外汇交易商的活动，但如果确实如此，必须以不损害社会利益的方式进行。正如哈特利·威瑟斯先生所说，通过建立自由市场，过去和今天的商人得以获得在其他情况下无法获得的汇票汇率，这也突显了投机证明对商业界有益的情况。然而，再次引用上述段落，当投机变成一种危险时，显然是采取行动的时候了。对此事最理智的看法可能来自处理进出口公司汇票的外汇经纪人，而在目前的局势下，有趣的是，据所知，交易所提供的更自由的市场抵消了更大的弊端。然而，在九江路有一些资金和知识规模较小的不负责任的元素在运作，如果政府意在消除这一部分，其行动并非没有正当理由。

登记。
请附入档案。
J.N.
1931年1月28日。

SPECIAL INQUIRY

THE CHINESE ECONOMIC BULLETIN.

JAN. 24, 1931.

Review of the Gold Bar Market

The gold bar market during the week ending January 17 showed a very unsettled tendency. Changes in quotations were so frequent and violent as to disturb very seriously the confidence of speculators. Affected by the easy conditions at the close of the preceding week and a rumour concerning the possibility of a big silver loan to China by the United States and Canada, the first two days of the week saw a sharp decline in prices. The excitement subsided on Wednesday, January 14, when purchasers greatly increased in number and were more active even than they were during the previous week. Quotations went steadily upward and toward the close of the week several new high records were established. Nevertheless, in spite of these rapid rises, the effect of frenzied trading on the part of dealers was such that even during one and the same session quotations dropped with the same suddenness as they had gone up. During the week-end session, fluctuations ranged as far apart as Tls. 33.50, an unprecedented record for a single session. The peak price of the week, Tls. 755.00, was reached on Saturday, January 17, while the bottom price, Tls. 686.00, was touched on Tuesday, January 13, representing a fluctuation of Tls. 69.00 as against Tls. 72.00 recorded during the preceding week.

Excited over the report that silver values might be stabilized by a big silver loan to China, the market on Monday, January 12, showed a sharp decline. It opened in the morning at Tls. 715.50 and soon rose to Tls. 724.80, but toward noon moved steadily downward and, after touching a low of Tls. 715.00, closed at noon at Tls. 719.50. During the afternoon, further depreciation was recorded. Despite an opening at Tls. 718.50 and a subsequent rise to Tls. 719.80, owing to bear activity quotations dropped sharply to Tls. 705.50, the bottom price of the day, before closing at Tls. 706.80. Owing to a current rumor that China had actually accepted a huge silver loan, the market on Tuesday, January 13, continued to slide rapidly. After business opened in the morning at Tls. 714.00, quotations steadily declined until Tls. 690.50 was reached at noon, after touching a high of Tls. 718.50 for the day. During the afternoon the drop in the market was particularly sharp. Opening at Tls. 691.50, rates dropped to Tls. 686.00, the week's bottom price, before business closed at Tls. 695.20. Between the high of the morning and the low of the afternoon, there was the astounding difference of Tls. 32.50.

As the result of another rumor concerning the absorption of a large amount of cash bars by a local bank, the market on Wednesday, January 14, recovered, and throughout the day quotations advanced, with the market showing a very sound tone. Business opened at Tls. 703.00 but quickly dropped to Tls. 697.00, but approaching noon a number of dealers came out as good buyers, and quotations moved gradually upward, closing firmly at noon at Tls. 706.20. The afternoon market showed a still stronger tendency, quotations soaring from an opening at Tls. 709.00 to hit the day's peak price at Tls. 720.50. The closing price receded slightly, being registered at Tls. 718.60. On Thursday, January 15, the market showed a strong opening but a weak close. Business began in the morning at Tls. 719.80, which was also the lowest price of the day, and closed in the afternoon at Tls. 729.50. The highest price touched was Tls. 737.50, representing a fluctuation of Tls. 17.70.

On Friday, January 16, the market was opened at 8:30 a.m. in order to allow time for carrying over accounts from February to March delivery. During the carry-over, owing to lack of buyers for cash bars, over-bought dealers were obliged to pay a premium to the bears of from Tls. 4.00 to Tls. 5.00 for each bar in order to carry their commitments forward from February to March. February delivery opened at Tls. 733.80 and after touching a high of Tls. 746.50, business closed at Tls. 735.50. Influenced by the jump in local exchange rates, business for March delivery opened with a strong bullish tendency. It opened in the morning at Tls. 738.50 and rose rapidly to Tls. 753.00, passing the previous record of Tls. 748.00 established on January 9, before business closed at noon at the latter figure. The new record was not long maintained as very uncertain feelings prevailed during the afternoon. Business opened at Tls. 746.50 and after touching a high of Tls. 746.50 and a low of Tls. 734.00, closed at Tls. 735.50. On Saturday, January 17, the fluctuation was more violent. As a result of the more rapid decline in silver prices abroad, the market opened at Tls. 745.50 and soon jumped to Tls. 755.00, the highest figure registered in local financial history.

金条市场回顾

截至1月17日的一周，金条市场显示出非常不稳定的趋势。报价变化如此频繁和剧烈，严重扰乱了投机者的信心。受前一周收盘时宽松状况以及有关美国和加拿大可能向中国提供大额白银贷款的谣言影响，本周头两天价格急剧下跌。1月14日星期三，兴奋情绪平息，买家数量大幅增加，甚至比上周更为活跃。报价稳步上升，接近周末时创下几个新高纪录。尽管如此，尽管迅速上涨，交易商的疯狂交易产生的影响使得即使在同一场交易中，报价也以与上涨同样的突然性下跌。在周末场次中，波动幅度高达关平银33.50两，创下单场交易的前所未有的纪录。本周最高价关平银755.00两于1月17日星期六达到，而最低价关平银686.00两于1月13日星期二触及，代表波动幅度为关平银69.00两，而前一周记录的波动幅度为关平银72.00两。

由于有关白银价值可能因向中国提供大额白银贷款而稳定的报告而感到兴奋，1月12日星期一的市场显示出急剧下跌。早盘以关平银715.50两开盘，很快涨至关平银724.80两，但临近中午时稳步下行，在触及关平银715.00两的低点后，午盘收于关平银719.50两。下午记录了进一步的贬值。尽管以关平银718.50两开盘并随后涨至关平银719.80两，但由于空头活动，报价急剧跌至关平银705.50两，即当日最低价，最后收于关平银706.80两。由于当前有谣言称中国实际上已接受了一笔巨额白银贷款，1月13日星期二的市场继续快速下滑。早盘业务以关平银714.00两开始后，报价稳步下降，直到中午触及当日高点关平银718.50两后达到关平银690.50两。下午市场跌幅尤为剧烈。以关平银691.50两开盘，汇率跌至关平银686.00两，即本周最低价，随后业务收于关平银695.20两。在上午的高点和下午的低点之间，有着令人震惊的关平银32.50两的差额。

由于另一则有关本地银行吸收大量现金金条的谣言，1月14日星期三的市场回升，全天报价上涨，市场显示出非常稳健的基调。业务以关平银703.00两开盘，但很快跌至关平银697.00两，但临近中午时，许多交易商作为优质买家出现，报价逐渐上行，午盘 firmly（坚挺）收于关平银706.20两。下午市场显示出更强的趋势，报价从开盘的关平银709.00两飙升至触及当日峰值关平银720.50两。收盘价略有回落，记录为关平银718.60两。1月15日星期四，市场显示强劲开盘但疲软收盘。早盘业务始于关平银719.80两，这也是当日最低价，下午收于关平银729.50两。触及的最高价为关平银737.50两，代表波动幅度为关平银17.70两。

1月16日星期五，市场于上午8:30开盘，以便有时间将账户从二月交割结转至三月交割。在结转期间，由于缺乏现金金条的买家，多头持仓的交易商被迫向空头支付每根金条关平银4.00至5.00两的溢价，以便将其承诺从二月结转至三月。二月交割以关平银733.80两开盘，在触及关平银746.50两的高点后，业务收于关平银735.50两。受本地汇率跳升的影响，三月交割业务开盘时显示出强烈的看涨趋势。早盘以关平银738.50两开盘，迅速涨至关平银753.00两，突破了1月9日创下的关平银748.00两的前纪录，随后午盘业务以后者数字收盘。这一新纪录维持时间不长，因为下午普遍存在非常不确定的情绪。业务以关平银746.50两开盘，在触及关平银746.50两的高点和关平银734.00两的低点后，收于关平银735.50两。1月17日星期六，波动更为剧烈。由于国外银价更快速的下跌，市场以关平银745.50两开盘，很快跳至关平银755.00两，这是本地金融史上记录的最高数字。

Their Reactions Under the Silver Slump
by B. Y. LEE

The far-reaching effects of the prevailing silver slump which is partially responsible for the world depression, is dealt with here by Mr. Lee in connection with the local financial institutions particularly the various exchanges' of which he mentioned six. Besides discussing the extraordinary reactions caused immediately by the unprecedented ebb in silver value, the writer gives in brief form pertinent information on the nature and the organization of the various exchanges as well as the manner of trading as employed in each case. While some of them do exist for the purpose of legitimate trade and investment, it is pointed out that a number of them are largely speculative in nature and for this reason the writer warns against rash adventures in this kind of business.

SPECULATION enters into the marketing of many staple commodities, gold and silver as well as stocks and bonds in all civilized countries, and China is no exception. Like most human institutions, speculation is neither wholly good nor wholly evil. Only those who have prepared themselves can hope to succeed, and then their success comes because of much thought, long experience, ample amount of capital, and persistent self-control. Speculation through the organized exchanges is strongly opposed in China, and very often no clear distinction is made between speculation and ordinary gambling. Practically all business men in Shanghai, Chinese and foreigners alike, have at one time or another speculated in one of the organised exchanges promoted by Chinese of which there are six in Shanghai, namely, The Shanghai Gold Bar Exchange, the Chinese Cotton Goods Exchange, the Shanghai Produce Exchange, the Chinese Bond Exchange, the Shanghai Oil and Bean Exchange and the Shanghai Flour Exchange. Many "society" men and women including many young ladies often speculate clandestinely and depend upon the telephone entirely in giving orders to the brokers to buy and sell. Thus they may make or lose a fortune without the knowledge of their friends or families. It is this class of speculators who suffer most in the end for they are as a rule losers.

The price of silver reached its lowest ebb in history on January 9 of this year when the white metal was quoted in London at 13¾ pence per ounce and the American dollar was quoted at 31- that is, Tls. 100 (Shanghai) for G.$31.75. The causes of the recent slump in silver are many; none of which can be controlled by China. Whenever there is a slight fluctuation of the white metal, it is indicated in the Shanghai Gold Bar Exchange at 2, Kiukiang Road, which, as its name indicates, is one of the largest and most popularised gambling establishments in the Orient ;it is a purely speculative market as the so-called gold bars that are dealt in are fictitious. The price of the fictitious gold bars is based on the local current exchange rate of yen (Japanese currency) multiplying by 48. For example, if to-day's rate is Tls. 150 for Y.100 the gold bar is quoted at Tls. 700. Of course, this calculation is purely a theoretical one, and many other factors influence the ups and downs of the bars during the course of a day's trading.

The Exchange is not a "traders' market," but rather a "speculative exchange" as there is no actual business being carried on. No speculators either take or deliver gold bars on settlement days which come the 16th of each month. Both buyers and sellers must "cover" their outstanding transactions on or before this day. On the average, the total number of fictitious gold bars transacted daily is about 100,000. But during the period of violent fluctuation as that happened during the last part of December and the first week of this year, more than a quarter of a million bars were transacted. The most violent fluctuation took place on January 6 to 9 of this year when the price of gold bars advanced from Tls. 650 to Tls. 748 during those 4 days. The profit or loss to speculators on those days was estimated to be around Tls. 6,500,000. Those 4 days were the most exciting ones in the history of the Exchange. A unit is of 7 bars, that is, one can either buy or sell any number of bars, in the multiple of 7. Officially, brokerage per unit of 7 bars is 7 maces or one mace per bar, but in actual practice half a mace per bar is accepted if the client is well known to the broker or he is doing a large amount of business.

On account of the quick fluctuation, many speculators, particularly the amateur speculators, are very fond of this game, for they can make a large fortune in a comparatively short time. There are many cycles in each year, and in each cycle a wide fluctuation of thirty or more taels per bar frequently occurs. In the summer of 1929 the gold bar was quoted around Tls. 400, and toward the end of that year it went to about 500 and in the summer of 1930 it went up to 625. 上海的投机机构
它们在银价暴跌下的反应
作者：B. Y. 李

李先生在此论述了当前银价暴跌的深远影响，此次暴跌部分导致了世界性经济萧条。他结合本地金融机构，特别是各类交易所的情况进行了阐述，文中提到了六家交易所。除了讨论因银价空前下跌而立即引发的异常反应外，作者还简要提供了关于各交易所的性质、组织形式以及各自采用的交易方式的相关信息。虽然其中一些交易所的存在是为了合法贸易和投资，但文章指出，许多交易所在很大程度上具有投机性质，因此作者警告人们不要在这种业务中轻率冒险。

在所有文明国家，投机行为都渗透在许多大宗商品、金银以及股票和债券的市场营销中，中国也不例外。像大多数人类制度一样，投机既非全然有益，也非全然有害。只有那些做好准备的人才有希望成功，而他们的成功源于深思熟虑、长期经验、充足的资本以及持久的自我控制。在中国，通过有组织的交易所进行的投机活动受到强烈反对，而且人们往往无法清楚地区分投机与普通赌博。实际上，上海的所有商人，无论是中国人还是外国人，都曾在由中国人 promoted（推广/创办）的有组织交易所中进行过投机，上海共有六家此类交易所，即：上海金条交易所、中国棉业交易所、上海证券物品交易所、中国债券交易所、上海油豆饼交易所和上海面粉交易所。许多“社交界”男女，包括许多年轻女士，经常秘密进行投机，完全依赖电话向经纪人下达买卖指令。因此，他们可能在朋友或家人不知情的情况下赚取或损失巨额财富。这类投机者最终遭受的损失最为惨重，因为他们通常是亏损者。

今年1月9日，银价跌至历史最低点，当时伦敦白银报价为每盎司13¾便士，美元汇率为31——即31.75美元兑换100两（上海规元）。近期银价暴跌的原因有很多，但没有一个是中国所能控制的。每当这种白色金属价格出现轻微波动时，位于九江路2号的上海金条交易所就会有所反映，正如其名所示，该所是东方最大且最流行的赌博场所之一；它是一个纯粹的投机市场，因为其中交易的所谓“金条”是虚构的。虚构金条的价格基于日元（日本货币）的当地现行汇率乘以48。例如，如果今天的汇率是100日元兑换150两，那么金条的报价就是700两。当然，这种计算纯属理论上的，在一天交易过程中，还有许多其他因素影响金条价格的涨跌。

该交易所不是一个“交易者市场”，而是一个“投机交易所”，因为没有实际业务在进行。在每月16日的结算日，没有任何投机者会提取或交付金条。买卖双方必须在此日期或之前“平仓”其未结交易。平均而言，每天交易的虚构金条总数约为10万条。但在剧烈波动期间，如去年12月下旬和今年第一周发生的情况，交易量超过25万条。最剧烈的波动发生在今年1月6日至9日，在这4天内，金条价格从650两上涨至748两。据估计，投机者在这几天的盈亏总额约为650万两。这4天是该交易所历史上最激动人心的日子。一个单位为7条，也就是说，人们可以买卖任何数量的金条，但必须是7的倍数。官方规定，每单位7条的佣金为7钱，即每条1钱，但在实际操作中，如果客户为经纪人所熟知或交易量巨大，每条5分的佣金也可被接受。

由于波动迅速，许多投机者，特别是业余投机者，非常喜欢这种游戏，因为他们可以在相对较短的时间内赚取巨额财富。每年有许多个周期，在每个周期中，每条金条经常会出现三十两或更多的宽幅波动。1929年夏天，金条报价在400两左右，那年年底涨至约500两，1930年夏天涨至625两。平均而言，投机者在单次操作中“玩”14到35条金条，碰巧的话，他一天可能赚取或损失多达500两。从1月5日到

During the “peaceful” days when the fluctuation in price is within a narrow limit, the margin money required for a unit of 7 bars is about Tls. 50, but during the “stormy” days, when the price fluctuates violently at more than ten taels a day, the margin required per unit may be as much as Tls. 150, depending upon the financial standing of the clients. During the busy hours the Exchange is crowded to the door with speculators, and very often the big speculators stand outside the Exchange building to give orders to their brokers even during the rainy days.

During the course of a year many rich men lost their fortune, while many office boys and clerks become quite wealthy by speculating in this Exchange. An interesting story of how a $15-clerk in a foreign bank has recently made a fortune in the speculation of gold bars has attracted wide gossiping among the speculators. Very frequently we read in newspapers that many a man jumps into the Whangpoo River or commits suicide on account of his failure in speculation. One of the richest young Chinese in Shanghai lost more than $30,000,-000 in this Exchange during the past two years.

The gold bar market is the most sensitive one. Practically speaking, every slight economic or political change in every country, particularly in Japan, China, and England at once affects the price. The causes that influence the ups and downs of gold bars are so numerous that only men of wide experience, who are well-informed in foreign exchange, especially in connection with Japan and China can cope with the situation. Even during the most peaceful days the fluctuation of price is from one to four or five taels per bar a day. For this reason there are many “scalpers” who can make a few taels a day in taking the advantage of slight fluctuations of the market. In the recent slump of silver many Chinese as well as foreign speculators were completely ruined. It is a well-known fact that every month or week new faces appear in the Exchange as the old faces are ruined and cannot go back there again.

During the past few years the import of cotton goods into China has been on the average more than $500,000,000 a year, a greater per cent. of which comes from Japan. Since last summer the price of yen has advanced from Tls. 110 to Tls. 155 in the Shanghai market. This means the imported yarn and cotton piece goods from Japan must be increased in price correspondingly. Then the manufactured yarn in Shanghai has also advanced from Tls. 135 per bale to Tls. 148. The raw cotton during the same period has advanced from Tls. 30.80 per picul in the middle of December to Tls. 35 in January 9 of this year, while the price of American cotton quoted on the New York Cotton Exchange has remained practically unchanged. The Cotton Goods Exchange was promoted by the Chinese cotton and yarn dealers and the cotton mill-owners. On the average the total number of bales of yarn transacted daily is 20,000, and that of cotton, 30,000 piculs.

The margin required per bale of yarn is six taels with 50 bales as a unit, and for cotton, three taels per picul with 100 piculs as a unit. Should the price either advance or drop one half of the margin money, the speculator is required to put up a second margin. The nominal commission charged per bale of yarn is half a tael and for a picul of cotton is 12/100 taels, or Tls. 12 per unit of 100 piculs, but this amount may be reduced by 50 per cent. depending upon the amount of business done and the character of the clients.

As a rule when the country is peaceful and the demand for yarn is normal, the price goes in full sympathy with American and Indian cotton and the Japanese yarn in Japan. Before quotations are fixed in the morning speculators first have to see the New York, Liverpool, Bombay and Osaka telegraphic quotations, and then the political and economic conditions of the country before taking any chance in buying or selling. These telegraphic quotations from abroad serve as price barometers, which constitute “inside information.” Very few shrewd speculators can ever get all the “inside information” in regard to the trend of the yarn price as there are many foreign as well as domestic factors governing its fluctuation. Externally, one should thoroughly understand the cotton market in America, India, and the yarn market in Japan as well as political conditions of these countries; internally, he should thoroughly understand the actual supply and demand of China cotton, the economic and political conditions of the country. Groundless rumours and sensational reports in the foreign press in regard to movements of troops often cause temporarily sharp decline in price. A sudden clamour of anti-Japanese movement gives the same effect. During this season the price of American cotton has been around ten cents a pound, and if not on account of the present silver slump, the China cotton would have sold for about Tls. 20 per picul instead of the prevailing price at Tls. 35 per picul. The high price of China cotton for this season has been entirely due to the high exchange rate in terms of silver. There must be some good reason if “breaks” come suddenly during the business hours and thoughtful speculators cannot sit down quietly and consider them meaningless.

A violent decline or advance of Tls. 30 per bale of yarn in a short time is a usual phenomenon in the Chinese yarn market. During the past three years, the fluctuation of price has not been very sharp on account of the steadiness of American cotton, which is a principal factor in governing the price of the China cotton. One who is ignorant of the American cotton market will be in the long run a loser. One reason why the Japanese speculators in the Chinese yarn and cotton market have been always successful is because they know the American market better than many Chinese cotton and yarn dealers do. An artful manipulation in the Cotton Goods Exchange by a few speculators has proved very powerful, and thousands of “outside” speculators have been “squeezed” out. 在一年当中，许多富人失去了财富，而许多办公室勤杂员和职员却通过在该交易所投机变得相当富有。最近，一家外国银行月薪15美元的职员如何通过金条投机发家致富的故事，在投机者中间引起了广泛的议论。我们经常从报纸上读到，许多人因投机失败而跳入黄浦江或自杀。上海最富有的年轻华人之一在过去两年中在该交易所损失了超过3,000万美元。

金条市场是最敏感的市场。 practically speaking（实际上），每个国家，特别是日本、中国和英国的任何轻微经济或政治变化，都会立即影响价格。影响金条涨跌的原因如此之多，只有那些经验丰富、精通外汇（尤其是涉及日本和中国的外汇）的人才能应对局势。即使在最平静的日子里，价格波动也是每天每条一两到四五两。因此，有许多“剥头皮者”（scalpers，指利用微小价差快速获利的短线交易者），他们可以利用市场的轻微波动每天赚取几两银子。在最近的银价暴跌中，许多中国及外国投机者彻底破产。众所周知，每个月或每周交易所里都会出现新面孔，因为旧面孔已经破产，无法再回到那里。

在过去几年中，输入中国的棉制品平均每年超过5亿美元，其中大部分来自日本。自去年夏天以来，日元在上海市场的汇率从110两上涨至155两。这意味着从日本进口的纱线和棉布价格必须相应提高。随后，上海生产的纱线价格也从每包135两上涨至148两。同期，原棉价格从去年12月中旬的每担30.80两上涨至今年1月9日的35两，而纽约棉花交易所报价的美棉价格基本保持不变。棉业交易所是由中国棉纱商和棉厂主推广创办的。平均而言，每天交易的纱线总数为2万包，棉花为3万担。

每包纱线所需的保证金为6两，以50包为一个单位；棉花每担保证金为3两，以100担为一个单位。如果价格上涨或下跌幅度达到保证金的一半，投机者需追加第二笔保证金。每包纱线的名义佣金为半两，每担棉花为12/100两，即每100担单位12两，但根据业务量和客户性质，这一金额可减少50%。

通常，当国家和平且纱线需求正常时，价格会与美棉、印棉以及日本的日纱价格完全同步。在早晨确定报价之前，投机者必须先查看纽约、利物浦、孟买和大阪的电报报价，然后考察国内的政治和经济状况，然后再决定买卖机会。这些来自国外的电报报价充当了价格晴雨表，构成了“内幕信息”。很少有精明的投机者能够获取有关纱线价格趋势的所有“内幕信息”，因为其波动受许多国内外因素支配。对外，人们应彻底了解美国、印度的棉花市场以及日本的纱线市场，以及这些国家的政治状况；对内，人们应彻底了解中国棉花的实际供需情况，以及国家的经济和政治状况。外国媒体关于军队调动毫无根据的谣言和耸人听闻的报道，往往会导致价格暂时急剧下跌。反日运动的突然爆发也会产生同样的效果。在这个季节，美棉价格一直在每磅10美分左右，如果不是因为当前的银价暴跌，中国棉花的售价应该是每担20两左右，而不是现行的每担35两。本季中国棉花的高价完全是由于以白银计算的高汇率所致。如果在营业时间内突然发生“崩盘”，必定有某种正当理由，深思熟虑的投机者不会静坐一旁并认为这些情况毫无意义。

在短时间内每包纱线剧烈下跌或上涨30两，是中国纱线市场的常见现象。在过去三年中，由于作为影响中国棉花价格主要因素的美棉价格稳定，价格波动并不十分剧烈。不了解美棉市场的人，长远来看将是输家。日本投机者在中国纱线和棉花市场上一直成功的原因之一，是他们比许多中国棉纱商更了解美国市场。少数投机者在棉业交易所中的巧妙操纵已被证明非常有力，成千上万的“场外”投机者被“挤压”出局。交易所有许多所谓的“金桶”（gold barrels，音译，指大户或庄家）在运作，他们拥有数……

The quotations of the Chinese Government
bonds in the Shanghai Bond Exchange, Hankow
Road, are the best barometer for interpreting Chi-
nese political and economic conditions. The bond mar-
ket is so sensitive that anything affecting the struc-
ture of the economic order of the country is indicat-
ed in the quotations of the bonds before the news
is known to the public or to newspaper correspon-
dents. The Exchange is truly a Chinese institution,
for it is almost entirely patronised by Chinese and
only a few foreigners are interested in this game.
For various reasons the Chinese stocks are not
quoted in this Exchange and only the Chinese Gov-
ernment bonds are dealt here. On the average the
total daily amount of transaction of bonds is about
$5,000,000 in their face value, and during the
period of uncertainty, as much as $20,000,000
of bonds have transacted. This Exchange
is not purely a speculative market as about
30 per cent. of the business is genuine; it is an
investor's market as well, for a majority of investors
come here to buy bonds for investment. The spot
goods are sold or bought with $1,000 face value as a
unit; the future, with $5,000 as a unit. The margin
money required for $5,000 unit is $300 with broker-
age of eight dollars. Should the price drop or advance
six dollars at any time during a day's business hours,
the operation is suspended for that day on that parti-
cular class of bonds. Of course, such a big drop or
advance has never taken place. All quotations are on
the dollar basis because the value of the bonds are
written in dollars.

Nearly all the government bonds are secured on
Customs duties with a few exceptions, such as the
Rolled Cigarette Bonds and 1928 Rehabilitation
Bonds which are secured on cigarettes and imported
kerosene oil. In time of peace and when gold is
low in terms of silver, the customs receipt is large,
which causes the price of these bonds to appre-
ciate in value or vice versa. In time when the
price of silver reached its lowest ebb, the custom
collection was greatly reduced. Naturally the price
of these bonds were affected. Due to the recent
slump in silver the so-called 6 Per Cent. Consolidated
bonds issued by the Peking Government and secur-
ed on the customs surplus dropped from $74 per
$100 face value on December 10, 1930 to $65 on
January 8 of this year, as many speculators thought
this bond might be irredeemable.

The bonds issued by the Peking Government
are called the "old bonds," and those issued by the
Nationalist Government are called the "new bonds."
The former generally bear 6 per cent. interest on
$100 face value, while the latter which constitute a
greater percentage of all the outstanding government
bonds, bear 8 per cent. to 10 per cent. a year. Many
of these new bonds are paid monthly. Generally
speaking, when the country is peaceful and the
customs receipt is normal, the price of these bonds
reaches as high as 95 per cent. Many conservative
investors prefer to buy the old bonds in spite of the
low interest, which are considered safer than the
new ones. In spite of the continuous civil wars
and the silver slump, all bonds that have been pro-
perly issued and well secured have been fully re-
deemed or are being redeemed. Before the govern-
ment had been removed to Nanking, the price of
these bonds quoted in the Shanghai Bond Exchange
always followed that quoted in the Peking Ex-
change, for Peking then was a principal source of
political and economic news, which governs the rise
and fall of bonds. Since Nanking has become the
capital, the Shanghai Bond Exchange has become
a national barometer for national bonds.

Except the amateur and reckless speculators,
any one who has some capital and experience can
make a fair living in buying these bonds whenever
they have dropped a few dollars per $100 face value,
and should the price continue dropping more, he can
keep them and draw interest, which amounts from
12 per cent. to 25 per cent. yearly depending upon
which class of bonds he chooses to buy. These bonds
can be mortgaged at a very good rate of interest
in any bank without difficulty. During the course
if 1929 and 1930, when the political conditions of
the country were unstable, the price of these bonds
dropped several times from $10 to $40 per $100
face value. As soon as the fighting mood of the
generals ceased temporarily, the price of these bonds
advanced again to their normal value.

In spite of heavy losses of fortune and
reputation, there is an unfailing stream of
"opportunity-seekers" flocking into these or-
ganised exchanges. Time and energy wast-
ed in these exchanges are parasitic activi-
ties, yet persons who are shrewd, experienced,
well-informed, with ample amount of capital, and
unusual ability for such operation, are in the long
run able to earn something in the nature of a pro-
fessional income. Many persons who are proud of
their learning and scholarship have generally failed
in this game as general education alone can not help
any one to be successful in such undertaking. Every
year large sums of money are lost in these organised
exchanges by incompetent speculators, who quit
the market and bear the loss whenever the market
is temporarily against them. Every person before

有数百万美元的资金可用于这种投机生意，他们经常联合起来，以临时信托的形式进行买卖。当市场行情有利时，他们会无限量地购买棉花或棉纱，并在每月月底几天的结算日接收货物；或者当市场低迷时，他们会卖出并交付货物，而普通投机者无法承接这些货物，从而在几天内造成人为的市场行情。

位于汉口路上海证券取引所的中国政府公债报价，是解读中国政治和经济状况的最佳晴雨表。债券市场对影响国家经济秩序结构的任何因素都极为敏感，在公众或新闻记者知晓消息之前，这些因素便已反映在债券报价中。该取引所确是一个华人机构，因为其客户几乎全为华人，只有少数外国人对这种游戏感兴趣。由于各种原因，华股不在该取引所挂牌，此处仅交易中国政府公债。平均而言，债券每日交易总额的面值约为500万美元，而在不确定时期，交易的债券金额高达2,000万美元。该取引所并非纯粹的投机市场，因为约30%的业务是真实的；它也是一个投资者市场，因为大多数投资者来此购买债券作为投资。现货交易以面值1,000美元为单位进行买卖；期货交易以5,000美元为单位。5,000美元单位所需的保证金为300美元，佣金为8美元。如果在一天营业时间的任何时候价格下跌或上涨6美元，则该特定种类债券的当日交易暂停。当然，如此大幅度的下跌或上涨从未发生过。所有报价均以美元为基础，因为债券的价值是以美元计值的。

几乎所有政府公债都以关税作为担保，仅有少数例外，如卷烟公债和1928年善后公债，它们分别以卷烟和进口煤油作为担保。在和平时期以及金价相对于银价较低时，关税收入丰厚，这会导致这些债券的价格升值，反之亦然。当银价跌至最低谷时，关税征收大幅减少。自然，这些债券的价格受到了影响。由于近期银价暴跌，由北京政府发行、以关税盈余为担保的所谓“六厘 Consolidated 公债”（即整理公债），其价格从1930年12月10日的每100美元面值74美元，跌至今年1月8日的65美元，因为许多投机者认为该债券可能无法赎回。

北京政府发行的债券被称为“旧债”，国民政府发行的债券被称为“新债”。前者通常按面值100美元支付6%的利息，而后者占所有未偿还政府公债的较大比例，年息为8%至10%。许多新债按月付息。一般而言，当国家和平且关税收入正常时，这些债券的价格可高达面值的95%。许多保守的投资者尽管利息较低，仍倾向于购买旧债，因为它们被认为比新债更安全。尽管内战不断且银价暴跌，所有发行得当且担保良好的债券均已全额赎回或正在赎回中。在政府迁往南京之前，上海证券取引所的这些债券报价总是跟随北京取引所的报价，因为当时北京是政治和经济新闻的主要来源，而这些新闻主导着债券的涨跌。自从南京成为首都后，上海证券取引所已成为全国公债的全国性晴雨表。

除了业余和鲁莽的投机者外，任何拥有一定资本和经验的人，都可以在这些债券每100美元面值下跌几美元时买入，从而维持体面的生活；如果价格继续下跌，他可以持有债券并收取利息，根据他选择购买的债券种类不同，年收益率在12%至25%之间。这些债券可以很容易地在任何银行以非常优惠的利率进行抵押。在1929年和1930年期间，当国内政治局势不稳定时，这些债券的价格数次从每100美元面值下跌10至40美元。一旦将军们的战意暂时平息，这些债券的价格便会再次回升至正常价值。

尽管遭受了巨大的财富和声誉损失，但仍有源源不断的“寻机者”涌入这些有组织的取引所。在这些取引所中浪费的时间和精力属于寄生性活动，然而，那些精明、经验丰富、消息灵通、拥有充足资本并具备非凡操作能力的人，从长远来看能够获得某种类似专业收入的收益。许多以学识和学问自豪的人通常在这场游戏中失败，因为仅凭一般教育无法帮助任何人在此类事业中取得成功。每年都有大量资金在这些有组织的取引所中被无能的投机者损失殆尽，当市场暂时对他们不利时，他们便退出市场并承担损失。每个人在试图在这些有组织的取引所中进行“生意”之前，都应多次认真考虑：他对他的“生意”了解多少，以及在不失社会“面子”的情况下，他能承受多大的损失。

Their Reactions Under the Silver Slump 
by B. Y. LEE 


The far-reaching effects of the prevailing silver slump which ts partially responsible for the 
world depression, ts dealt with here by Mr. Lee in connection with the local financial institutions 
particularly the various exchanges‘of which he mentioned siz. Besides discussing the extraordin- 
ary. reactions caused immediately by the unprecedented ebb in silver value, the writer gives in 
brief, form pertinent information on the nature and the organtzation of the various exchanges as 
well as the manner of trading as employed in each case. While some of them do exist for the pur- 
pose of legitimate trade and investment, it ts pointed out that a number of them are largely 
speculative in nature and for this reason the writer warns against rash adventures in this kind 


of business, 


PECULATION enters into the marketing of 

many staple commodities, gold and silver as 
well as stocks and bonds in all civilized countries, 
and China is no exception. Like most human in- 
stitutions, speculation ie neither wholly good nor 
wholly evil. Only those who have prepared them- 
selves can hope to succeed, and then their success 
comes because of much thought, long experience, 
ample amount of capital, and persistent eelf-con- 
trol. Speculation through the organized exchanges 
is strongly opposed in China, and very often no 
clear distinction is made between speculation and 
ordinary gambling. Practically all business men in 
Shanghai, Chinese and foreigners alike, have at 
one time or another speculated in one of the organis- 
ed exchanges promoted by Chinese of which there are 
six in Shanghai, namely, The Shanghai Gold Bar 
Exchange, the Chinese Cotton Goods Exchange. 
the Shanghai Produce Exchange, the Chinese Bond 
Exchange, the Shanghai Oil and Bean Exchange 
and the Shanghai Flour Exchange. Many 
‘society’? men and women including many young 
ladies often speculate clandestinely and depend 
upon the telephone entirely in giving orders to the 
‘brokers to buy and sell. Thus they may make or 
lose a fortune without the knowledge of their friends 
or families. It is this class of speculators who 
suffer most in the end for they are as a rule losers. 


The price of silver reached ite lowest ebb in his- 
tory on January 9 of this year when the white metal 
was quoted in London at 13} pence per ounce 
and the American dollar was quoted at 31-2 that 
is, Tle. 100 (Shanghai) for G.$31.75. The 
causes of the eecent slump in silver are many ; 
none of which can be controlled by China. When- 
ever there is a slight fluctuation of the white 
metal, it is indicated in the Shanghai Gold Bar 
Exchange at 2, Kiukiang Roed, which, as its name 
indicates, is one of the largest and most popularis- 
ed gambling establighments in the Orient ;it isa pute- 
ly speculative market as the so-called gold bars that 
are dealt in are fictitious. The price of the ficti- 
tious gold bars is based on the local current ex- 
change rate of yen (Japanese currency) multipling 


by 48. For example, if to-day's rate is Tis. 150 
for Y.100 the gold bar is quoted at Tls. 700. 
Of course, this calculation is purely a theoretical 
one, and many other factors influence the ups and 
downs of the bars during the course of a day's 
trading. 

The Exchange is not a ‘‘traders’ market,’ but 
rather a ‘‘speculative exchange’’ as there is no- 
actual business being carried on. No speculators 
either take or deliver gold bars:on settlement days 
which come the 16th of each month. Both buyers 
and sellers must ‘‘cover’’ their outstanding transac- 
tions on or before this day. On the average, the 
total number of fictitious gold bars transacted daily 
is about 100,000. But during the period of violent 
fluctuation as that happened during the last part 
of December and the first week of thie year, more 
than a quarter of a million bars were transacted. 
The most violent fluctuation took place on January 
6 to 9 of this year when the price of gold bars 
advanced from Tls. 650 to Tis. 748 during those 4 
lays. The profit or loss to speculators on 
days was estimated to be around Ts. 6,500,000. 
Those 4 days were the most exciting ones in the 
history of the Exchange. A unit is of 7 bars, that 
is, one can either buy or sell any number of bars, 
in the multiple of 7. Officially, brokerage per unit 
of 7 bars is 7 maces or one mace per bar, but in 


actual practice half a mace per bar is accepted if the 


client is well known to the broker or he is doing a 
large amount of business. 

On account of the quick fluctuation, many — 
speculators, particularly the amateur speculators, 
are very fond of this game, for they can make a 
large fortune in a comparatively ebort time. There 
are many cycles in each year, and in each cycle a 
wide fluctuation of thirty or more taels per bar 
frequently occurs. In the summer of 1929 the 
gold bar was quoted around Tis. 400, and toward 
the end of that year it went to about 500 and in 
the sammer of 1930 it went up to 625. On the - 
average, speculator ‘‘plays’’ from 14 to 35 bars in 
8 single operation, and by chance he may make or 
lose as much as Tis. 500 a day. From January 5 to 


9, it went up from 676 to 748—the biggest jump that 
has ever been recorded in the Exchange since its 
existence in such a short time. During the ‘‘peace- 
ful’’ days when the fluctuation in price is within s 
narrow limit, the margin money required for a unit 
of 7 bars is about Tls. 50, but during the ‘‘stormy”’ 
days, when the price fluctuates violently at more 
than ten taels a day, the margin required per unit 
may be as much as Tis. 150, depending upon the 
financial standing of the clients. During the busy 
hours the Exchange is crowded to the door with 
speculators, and very often the big speculators 
stand outside the Exchange building to give orders 
to their brokers even during the rainy days. 

During the course of a year many rich men 
lost their fortune, while many office boys and clerks 
become quite wealthy by speculating in this Ex- 
change. <An interesting story of how  $15- 
clerk in a foreign bank has recently made a fortune 
in the speculation of gold bars has attracted wide 
gossiping among the speculators. Very frequently 
we read in newspapers that many a man jumps into 
the Whangpoo River or commits suicide on account 
of his failure in speculation. One of the richest 
young Chinese in Shanghai lost more than $30,000,- 
000 in this Exchange during the past two years. 

The gold bar market is the most sensitive one. 
Practically speaking, every slight economic or politi- 
cal change in every country, particularly in Japan, 
China, and England at once affects the price. The 
causes that influence the ups and downs of gold 
bars are so numerous that only men of wide ex- 
perience, who are well-informed in foreign ex- 
change, especially in connection with Japan 
and China can cope with the situation. Even 
during the most peaceful days the fluctuation of 
price ia from one to four or five taels per bar a 
day. For this reason there are many ‘‘scalpers’’ 
who can make a few taels a day in taking the ad- 
vantage of slight fluctuations of the market. In 
the recent slump of silver many Chinese as, well 
as foreign speculators were completely ruined. It 
is a well-known fact that every month or week
